correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed over all a,b,c,d>=1: CRT decomposes U(n) into prime-power unit groups; Frattini reduction to exponents 3,2,2,2 preserves generation in every primary quotient. The 2-primary rank matrices have determinants 1,-1,-3 and the 3-primary minor determinant -2; the 5 and 7 entries 16 mod5 and 40 mod7 are nonzero. Lower bounds use exactly 3,4,5 independent quadratic characters with an explicit 11+13+17 dependence in the a=1 case. Direct integer computation independently verifies discrete logs, 24 rank cases, six subgroup orders. Neither computation nor any finite bound replaces infinite lifting.

originality.rationale: The published October 2026 primary source gives average and almost-all upper bounds for the same least-generator invariant, not the sharp 19/23 identity uniformly over all positive exponents of 2,3,5,7. A classical Frattini/CRT reduction does not supply the specific exact cutoff or its proof without local prime-order character ranks. Semantic searches of the published mathematical records and web searches for aliases, exact values and prime-power stability found no covering theorem. The 1993 full text is inaccessible; a possible implicit classification or historical exact table is a residual risk rather than a demonstrated implication.

value.rationale: This determines a natural exact generator-threshold invariant for the full unbounded exponent family supported on the first four primes. It identifies a sharp jump from 19 to 23 at a=3 and complete independence from all odd-prime exponents, a precise new behavior not supplied by general average upper bounds. The 7-component couples additional 3-character information to the 2-character rank and makes the constant evaluation mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary one-modulus exercise. Future small-generator testing can use the exact infinite benchmark, without asserting further arithmetic applications.
